objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## Six measured attempts on the frozen baseline, and what they rule out

Every number is measured with the same frozen protocol (Stage 2: 3000 epochs, four cards;
Stage 3: 150 epochs, width-20 beam, 57,439 test rows).

| what was tried on `TIGER_RQ-VAE` | SID structure (L1/L2/L3) | Stage 3 R@10 |
|---|---|---|
| nothing (the frozen baseline itself) | 247/7414/20223 | **0.055537** |
| successor-entropy curvature at T1 (#124) | 256/3952/13702 | 0.050628 |
| successor prototype + tangent residual (T1) | 238/7223/20418 | 0.054249 |
| coarse geodesic first level (26 codes) | 26/1761/15069 | 0.054858 |
| + curved behaviour-ordered extension token | 28/1751/14354 | 0.055293 |
| successor residual barycenter at T2/T3 | 187/7083/18005 | 0.054353 |
| capacity budget (32, 96, 256) | 28/1044/11922 | 0.054023 |

**None of them beats the baseline.** The per-position forensics say why: every one of these
mechanisms changed the *structure* of the SID space (how many codes per level, how balanced
the buckets are) and left the *semantic partition* — which item shares a prefix with which
other item — as content-only as the baseline's. The arms that do reach 0.062-0.064 have the
same structure statistics as the baseline but a behaviourally coherent partition: their gold
prefix survives depth 1 and 2 almost always (1.000 and 0.829 in `l1_only`), and their
recall follows that survival, not any bucket statistic.

So the remaining lever is the **partition itself**: which items are neighbours in the ball.
This round must change that with a learning signal, not with a capacity or assignment tweak.

## What the mechanism must be

A **behaviour-contrastive objective on the curved representation**: the train-only directed
successor structure defines positive pairs (an item and its observed next targets, or items
that are next targets of the same cohort) and negative pairs (items never adjacent in any
training history); the objective pulls positives together and pushes negatives apart *in the
hyperbolic ball where the quantizer assigns codes*, so the consequence is that behaviourally
coherent items fall into the same coarse prefix and behaviourally unrelated items do not.

Requirements:

* the contrastive term must act on the *same* representation the quantizer clusters (not on a
  side branch), and its gradient must reach the encoder and the first two codebooks;
* the geodesic distance of the curved space must be the metric the contrastive term uses, and
  the curvature must be a stated function of the train-only branching statistic;
* the mechanism must state its capacity budget and why the partition it induces keeps the
  first two positions cheap (target: gold prefix alive above 0.95 at depth 1 and above 0.8 at
  depth 2, as the two 0.062 arms measure);
* behaviour-off (shuffled successor pairs) and geometry-off (Euclidean contrastive distances
  with the same pairs) are the required ablations.

Out of scope: any objective that only re-weights an existing assignment cost; any change that
leaves the assignment identical (a monotone per-row rescaling cannot change an argmin); any
mechanism whose gradient into the encoder is zero at initialisation *and* stays zero.

## Required measurement contract

State the predicted direction of `L1 Hard ER` (canonical 52,855 pairs, ten fixed negatives),
gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4, teacher-forced top-1 accuracy of T1..T4, and Stage 3
`test_R@10`. The reference to beat is 0.055537 (the baseline control) and the target is 0.065.

## Frozen constraints

Four tokens with the deterministic collision-extension token, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four
cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no validation or
test behaviour in SID construction. The one-epoch smoke must stay near the baseline's cost
(0.13 s/epoch) and must show a non-zero gradient into the encoder on the real batch.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

findings.correction: Implement the specified sparse successor distributions and cosine-over-union thresholding, use the stated one-positive/eight-negative objective, construct differentiable first-two-level quantized prefix points, and use branching-conditioned curvature/geodesic scoring on that shared prefix representation. findings.detail: There is a connected behaviour/curved-distance loss path, but it does not implement the specified mechanism faithfully. Behaviour supports are row-L2-normalized then compared by dot product, not successor probability distributions with cosine on their union as specified (these coincide only for nonempty rows). It mines one negative per source, not eight, and contrasts a soft first-level codeword distribution rather than differentiable first-two-level quantized prefix points. The branching statistic is computed but only weakly enters a fixed curvature formula; it does not condition a branching prefix representation. The configured codebooks are three levels [32,256,256], not the required four [256,256,256,256].

The candidate positive/negative construction returns exactly one negative per row (lines 264-273); _soft_prefix accesses only vq_layers[0] (lines 309-316); _tokenizer_config uses CODEBOOK_NUM=3 and CODEBOOK_SIZE=(32,256,256) (lines 79-84). No second-level prefix point participates.

This prevents the required behaviour-off causal comparison. The live curved branch otherwise has a differentiable path through softmax weights and codebook distances into encoder/codebook parameters; no claim of runtime smoke is made.

findings.correction: L2-normalize each sparse probability row before multiplying (with zero-row safeguards) to compute cosine and apply the stated threshold/top-one rule. Add the reverse anchor direction and average the two directional NCE terms to make the loss symmetric.
findings.detail: The proposal requires cosine similarity between successor probability rows, but pair mining computes the raw sparse dot product `supports @ supports.T`. Since rows are L1-normalized probabilities, this is not cosine similarity (which additionally divides by each row's L2 norm). Consequently the 0.2 threshold and selected positive pairs do not implement the specified cohort relation. Additionally, the contrast is anchor-to-positive only rather than symmetric as the CHANGE requires.
findings.reproduction: For two identical distributions `[0.5, 0.5]`, raw dot is 0.5 while cosine is 1; for distributions `[1, 0]` and `[0.5, 0.5]`, raw dot is 0.5 while cosine is about 0.707. These yield different scores/rankings, and rows with different support concentration can cross the 0.2 threshold under raw dot despite their cosine being below it. Inspect `_mine_pairs`: `similarity = supports @ supports.T` at line 257 and threshold at 264. The single direction is directly visible in the one `F.cross_entropy` call at 361.

findings.correction: Build minibatches of mined source-positive pairs (and sampled negatives) or otherwise ensure each training step draws usable pairs from the whole precomputed list; avoid the global 512-anchor truncation as the only source of behavior supervision. Add a guard/metric that detects zero usable pairs and verify gradients on encoder and both prefix codebooks in the prescribed smoke.
findings.detail: Pair mining caps the entire dataset's pair list at 512 (NCE_MAX_PAIRS), then each minibatch discards every pair unless both source and positive and at least one negative occur in that same batch. With item-level shuffled batches, a valid mined pair need not ever co-occur; when none does, _contrastive_term returns encoded.sum()*0 and the purported mechanism has no gradient/update for that step. The specification calls for a positive and eight negatives per anchor in the minibatch prefix path, not a globally capped sparse subset that can silently become a dead term. A zero contrastive term is finite, so the existing finite-loss check does not detect this failure.

A batch containing only items outside the 512 cached anchors has the same result.

scores.counterexample: For q=0, exp_0(q)=0 regardless of c; if all sampled prefixes are zero, changing the behavior-derived curvature cannot change pair distances or gradients, so the claimed curvature pathway has no effect in that case.
scores.objection: This is very close computationally to the measured successor-geodesic-coarse family, and the bundle shows that family underperformed stronger measured alternatives on beam Recall; the new contrastive objective may not cure that failure mode.
scores.rationale: E5 gives auditable train-only entropy stratification and supports the branching hypothesis (4). Curved distance on the actual quantized prefix is real, but no matched-control argument or cancellation analysis establishes necessity (3). The change is a routine transition-geodesic contrastive variant of measured successor-geodesic methods (2; E6). Assignment gradients could plausibly change T1/T2 and next-token survival (4), but no explicit matched three-way controls/failure criterion are specified (2). Formula and cost are present, but stable ball projection, distance clipping, and denominator safeguards are absent (2). E6 makes this a near-repeat of a measured negative (1).
scores.scope_reason: Behavior and curvature are coupled through the quantized prefix and expected effects are stated, but it does not name the required behavior-off, Euclidean/geometry-off, and both-on comparison; it also omits numerical safeguards for the Poincare map/distance.
